A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same Visual-TCAV paper, with matching scientific sections, equations, seven figures and references. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; separately mentioned supplementary material is not included in either file.

before.justification: Sections 4.2-4.4 report original local and global explanations, controlled experiments with tagged images, classifier accuracies, concept attributions and comparisons with TCAV.

after.justification: The same original empirical results remain in Sections 4.2-4.4 and Figures 3-7, including the controlled tagging experiment and TCAV comparison.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1-3.3 retain the same difference-of-means CAV construction, spatial pooling, concept-map normalization and Integrated Gradients attribution with spatial masking. No algorithmic component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions retain ImageNet and CelebA classification, concept examples from DTD, image searches and Stable Diffusion, and the cucumber/taxi/zebra tagging experiment. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Section 4.4.1 retains TCAV as the quantitative comparator. Section 4.4 also retains the same reported qualitative checks using Grad-CAM and IG; comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: The architectures, sample counts, 300 integration steps, 200 images per global explanation, and five training conditions with 0%, 25%, 50%, 75% and 100% tagged images remain unchanged. No evaluation procedure is revised.

E4.justification: The layer-wise analyses, misclassification and bias examples, and controlled investigation of reliance on entities versus tags are retained unchanged in Sections 4.2-4.4 and Figures 3-7.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the error bars in Figures 5-6 and Figure 7's exclusion of statistically insignificant TCAV scores with p-value greater than 0.05. No run counts, seed information or statistical reporting procedures are added.

E6.justification: The result images, numerical entries and qualitative findings are identical. For example, Section 4.4.1 retains accuracies on untagged images of 96.5%, 96.2%, 96.2%, 95.2% and 36.2%. Figure 6 is relocated without changing its results.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(2), the normalization definitions, the qualification that concept attributions need not be additive, and the Integrated Gradients completeness reasoning remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: concept localization and attribution for local and global CNN explanations, supported by controlled validation. The claimed advantage over TCAV is unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning shortcut learning, class selectivity and misclassifications are unchanged. Section 5.1 retains the limitations concerning concept-example collection and positive-only multiclass attribution, together with the same proposed extensions.

D1.justification: The abstract changes from promising that code will be available soon to stating its availability and providing a repository link. Section 4.1's hardware, software versions, computation times and implementation settings are unchanged.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 45 works and retain the same positioning relative to TCAV, saliency methods and other concept-based approaches. Changed reference back-page numbers reflect pagination only.

P1.justification: V2 revises the abstract's code-availability sentence, adds an equal-contribution footnote for the first two authors, and removes the detailed Contribution Statement. The scientific prose and section order otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 6 moves from page 7 to page 8, placing it above Figure 7, while text, section starts and references reflow. All seven figures retain their content and captions within the same two-column format.

improvement.justification: Replacing the future code-release promise with a concrete repository link modestly improves reproducibility documentation. Scientific evidence is unchanged. Removing detailed contributor roles creates a small transparency loss, but the code-access information provides a limited net benefit. Repository contents cannot be assessed from these PDFs.
